question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The relentless march of digital omnipresence has fundamentally altered the ontological structure of human interaction, rendering genuine connection increasingly (1)_____. We find ourselves ensnared in a web of algorithmic validation, where our self-worth is inherently tied to the capricious metrics of virtual engagement. This shift from authentic existence to curated performance is not merely an innocuous evolution but a profound (2)_____ of our subjective reality. Consequently, individuals are left grappling with a pervasive sense of existential dread, as the boundaries between the physical self and the digital avatar become dangerously (3)_____. The philosopher's task, therefore, is no longer solely to interpret the world but to actively (4)_____ the insidious ways in which technology colonizes our consciousness. Failure to do so risks a dystopic future where human agency is completely (5)_____ to the whims of the machine. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
explanation: Passage ka tone deep aur highly critical hai. Author bol raha hai ki digital duniya ki wajah se asli human connection lagbhag unreal ya impossible ho gaya hai. 'Chimerical' ka matlab hota hai purely imaginary ya unreal. 'Palpable' (tangible) aur 'quintessential' (perfect example) positive/real hain, jo tone ke opposite hain. 'Perfunctory' (routine) contextually fit nahi hota.
trick: Sentence ka starting 'relentless march' aur 'altered' negative vibe de raha hai. Positive aur neutral options ko turant eliminate kar do.
tip: Negative passage mein unreal ya fading meaning wale words dhoondhein.

question: Based on the passage in Question 1, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
explanation: Yahan 'authentic existence' se 'curated performance' ki taraf shift ki baat ho rahi hai, jisko author ek destructive act manta hai. 'Subversion' ka matlab hota hai kisi established system ya reality ko undermine karna ya barbaad karna. 'Apotheosis' (climax/highest point) aur 'vindication' (justification) positive terms hain. 'Exegesis' (critical explanation) yahan grammar aur logic dono mein fail hota hai.
trick: Pichla phrase 'not merely an innocuous evolution' hint karta hai ki aage koi extreme negative word aayega.
tip: Innocuous (harmless) ka contrast hamesha destructive hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 1, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
explanation: Passage mein physical self aur digital avatar ke beech ka fark mitne ki baat ho rahi hai. Jab boundaries weak ho jati hain aur cheezein aar-paar hone lagti hain, toh unhe 'porous' (having holes/permeable) kaha jata hai. 'Demarcated' (clearly defined), 'sacrosanct' (pavitra/untouchable), aur 'immutable' (unchangeable) sab strong boundaries ko dikhate hain.
trick: Agar do alag identities mix ho rahi hain, toh unki boundary weak (porous) hi hogi, strong nahi.
tip: Mixing of identities implies weakening of borders.

question: Based on the passage in Question 1, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
explanation: Philosopher ka naya task kya hona chahiye? Technology ke bure tareeqon ko samajhna aur unse sawaal karna. 'Interrogate' yahan exactly question/analyze karne ke sense mein use hua hai. 'Obfuscate' (confuse) aur 'exacerbate' (worsen) philosopher kyun karega? 'Placate' (pacify) technology ko shant karne ka koi sense nahi banta.
trick: Philosopher ka kaam humesha analyze, question ya interpret karna hota hai, isliye 'interrogate' sabse logical verb hai.
tip: Intellectual task hamesha questioning ya analysis se juda hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 1, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
explanation: Sentence ek dystopic future ki baat kar raha hai jahan humans machines ke ghulam ban jayenge. 'Subjugated' ka matlab hota hai under control ya dominated. 'Recalcitrant' (stubbornly disobedient) aur 'imperious' (arrogant/domineering) toh insaan ko strong dikhayenge, jo 'whims of the machine' wale context se match nahi karta.
trick: Blank ke baad 'to the whims' likha hai. 'Subjugated to' ek standard colocation hai jiska matlab dusre ke ishare par chalna hai.
tip: 'To the whims of' ke pehle hamesha submission wala word aayega.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: In contemporary epistemological discourse, the very concept of objective truth has been subjected to a relentless barrage of relativistic critique. We have entered a paradigm where factual accuracy is often considered (6)_____ to emotional resonance or ideological alignment. This (7)_____ of reality allows disparate echo chambers to construct mutually exclusive narratives, each masquerading as absolute certainty. The danger lies not merely in the proliferation of falsehoods, but in the deliberate (8)_____ of the intellectual scaffolding required to discern fact from fiction. When empirical evidence is routinely dismissed as partisan fabrication, the foundation of democratic deliberation becomes severely (9)_____. To navigate this labyrinth of cognitive dissonance, one must cultivate a radical form of intellectual humility, resisting the seductive allure of (10)_____ dogmas. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 6.
explanation: Author bol raha hai ki aaj ke time mein facts ki value emotions se kam ho gayi hai. 'Subordinate to' ka matlab hota hai kisi se inferior ya lower rank ka hona. 'Paramount' (supreme) ulta meaning dega. 'Germane' (relevant) aur 'antithetical' (opposite) yahan comparison ka logic set nahi kar paate.
trick: Sentence mein 'often considered... to emotional resonance' likha hai. Post-truth era mein emotions facts par dominate karte hain, toh facts 'subordinate' ho gaye.
tip: Jahan facts ignore hote hain, wahan unki position subordinate hoti hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 6, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 7.
explanation: Aage likha hai 'disparate echo chambers' aur 'mutually exclusive narratives', matlab reality ke alag-alag tukde ho gaye hain jo aapas mein match nahi karte. 'Bifurcation' ka matlab splitting into branches ya fractions hota hai. 'Consonance' (agreement) aur 'amalgamation' (merging) iske bilkul opposite hain.
trick: Agar narratives 'mutually exclusive' (ek dusre se alag) hain, toh reality jud nahi rahi, balki toot rahi hai. Split wala word dhoondho.
tip: Echo chambers hamesha division (bifurcation) create karte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 6, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 8.
explanation: Yahan ek danger (khatre) ki baat ho rahi hai jahan fact aur fiction ke beech fark karne wale intellectual system ko deliberately toda ja raha hai. 'Dismantling' ka matlab hota hai destroy ya take apart karna. 'Fortification' (strengthening) toh positive ho jayega. 'Lionization' (glorify karna) aur 'reification' (abstract ko real banana) out of context hain.
trick: 'Danger lies in...' ke baad wale phrase mein intellectual structure ke destroy hone ka negative action hi aayega.
tip: Scaffolding (structure) ko hatane ke liye 'dismantling' use hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 6, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 9.
explanation: Agar empirical evidence ko fake maan liya jaye, toh democracy ka foundation kharab ya corrupt ho jayega. 'Vitiated' ka matlab hota hai spoil, impair, ya quality destroy karna. 'Ennobled' (respected banana) aur 'galvanised' (excite/stimulate karna) positive hain. 'Entrenched' (firmly established) yahan negative consequence nahi dikhata.
trick: Foundation ke 'severely' ke baad koi destructive aur negative consequence hi aayega.
tip: Democratic foundation kharab hone ko 'vitiated' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 6, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 10.
explanation: Passage end mein humein 'cognitive dissonance' se bachne ke liye absolute certainty waale beliefs se door rehne ki salah deta hai. 'Infallible dogmas' wo hote hain jo dawa karte hain ki wo kabhi galat nahi ho sakte. 'Empirical' toh evidence-based hota hai jisko author support karta hai. 'Solipsistic' (only self exists) aur 'heuristic' (trial and error) yahan dogma ke nature ko define nahi karte.
trick: Dogmas hamesha yeh claim karte hain ki wo 100% true hain. 'Infallible' ka matlab hota hai incapable of making mistakes.
tip: Dogma ke sath hamesha absolute ya infallible jaise words aate hain.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The trajectory of avant-garde aesthetics over the past century has arguably been characterized by a gradual departure from the pursuit of the sublime towards a relentless fixation on provocation. Much of contemporary art seems to operate under the assumption that to be profoundly meaningful, a work must first be deeply (11)_____. Consequently, galleries are frequently inundated with installations that prioritize visceral shock over contemplative depth, reducing the spectator's role to that of a passive consumer of manufactured outrage. This transactional relationship fundamentally (12)_____ the traditional contract between artist and audience, replacing quiet introspection with a cacophony of performative transgression. Yet, amidst this landscape of relentless sensationalism, one occasionally encounters pieces that manage to (13)_____ the superficiality of their medium. These rare creations serve as poignant reminders that art's highest calling is not merely to disrupt, but to offer a fleeting (14)_____ from the banal realities of existence, ultimately guiding us back to a state of profound (15)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 11.
explanation: Passage modern art ke 'provocation' aur 'shock' value ki baat kar raha hai. Art works aaj kal pehle logon ko shock dena chahte hain. 'Jarring' ka matlab hota hai shocking, disturbing ya unpleasant. 'Edifying' (moral improvement dene wala) purane art ka feature tha. 'Sycophantic' (chaploosi) aur 'lackadaisical' (lazy) bilkul irrelevant hain.
trick: Agle sentence mein 'visceral shock' likha hai. Jarring aur shock synonymous ideas hain.
tip: Shock aur provocation ka closest synonym 'jarring' hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 11, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 12.
explanation: Contemporary art artist aur audience ke puraane shaant rishte ko khatam kar raha hai aur uski jagah outrage la raha hai. 'Repudiates' ka matlab hota hai deny karna, reject karna ya tod dena. 'Bolsters' (support karna), 'vindicates' (justify karna) aur 'reiterates' (repeat karna) yahan galat meaning de rahe hain kyunki traditional relation toot raha hai.
trick: 'Replacing' word indicate karta hai ki purani cheez ko hataya ya reject kiya ja raha hai, isliye negative verb chahiye.
tip: Old contract ko break karne ke liye 'repudiates' lagao.

question: Based on the passage in Question 11, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 13.
explanation: Par in sab sensationalism ke beech, kuch rare pieces aese hote hain jo is superficiality (chhichhore-pan) se upar uth jaate hain. 'Transcend' ka matlab hota hai go beyond the limits. 'Capitulate' (surrender), 'emulate' (copy) aur 'exacerbate' (worsen) rare aur achhi art piece ki quality nahi ho sakti.
trick: Sentence ki shuruaat 'Yet' se hui hai, yani ab positive baat hogi jo negative superficiality ko hara degi.
tip: 'Yet' ke baad superficiality ko beat karne wala positive word aayega.

question: Based on the passage in Question 11, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 14.
explanation: Asli art ka kaam sirf disturb karna nahi, balki boring aur ordinary (banal) zindagi se thodi der ki shanti ya rahat dena hai. 'Reprieve' ka matlab temporary relief ya aaram hota hai. 'Indictment' (aarop) aur 'harbinger' (sign of future) yahan fit nahi hote.
trick: 'Fleeting' (kuch der ka) ke sath hamesha relief ya aaram ka concept fit hota hai jab situation 'banal realities' ki ho.
tip: Boring reality se humein temporary 'reprieve' chahiye hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 11, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 15.
explanation: Great art ke end mein audience ko kis state mein jaana chahiye? Ek shanti aur mental balance ki state mein. 'Equanimity' ka matlab hota hai mental calmness aur composure. 'Turbulence' (ashanti) aur 'despondency' (nirasha) passage ke uplifting conclusion ko contradict karte hain.
trick: 'Guiding us back to' aur pichla word 'reprieve' hint de rahe hain ki last word ultimate peace ka hoga.
tip: Art ka ultimate positive psychological effect 'equanimity' hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The phenomenon of hyper-urbanization presents a compelling sociological paradox: never before have human beings lived in such dense proximity, yet experienced such profound psychological (16)_____. The architectural geography of the modern metropolis, characterized by towering monoliths of glass and steel, seems designed to actively (17)_____ communal interaction, fostering a culture of atomized individualism. Citizens navigate these concrete canyons not as members of a cohesive community, but as isolated monads, their gazes averted, their interactions strictly transactional. This pervasive alienation is further compounded by the socioeconomic stratifications that create invisible but (18)_____ barriers between different classes. The city, once idealized as a crucible of democratic assimilation, has increasingly devolved into a fragmented landscape of exclusive enclaves and marginalized peripheries. Unless we radically reimagine our urban spaces to prioritize human connection over mere functional efficiency, we risk cementing a societal structure where genuine empathy becomes a rare and (19)_____ commodity, ultimately leading to the slow but inevitable (20)_____ of the civic spirit. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 16.
explanation: Ek paradox (virodhabhas) bataya gaya hai: log physically paas hain ('dense proximity'), phir bhi mentally alag aur akele hain. 'Alienation' ka matlab isolation ya akelapan hota hai. 'Assimilation' (mil jana) aur 'gregariousness' (sociability) toh proximity ke saath normal hain, paradox nahi banate.
trick: 'Yet' ke pehle 'dense proximity' (nearness) hai, toh 'yet' ke baad doori ya akelapan hi aayega.
tip: Proximity (paas hona) ka paradox hamesha alienation (doori) hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 16, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 17.
explanation: Modern architecture logon ko akele rehne ('atomized individualism') par majboor karta hai. Iska matlab architecture communal interaction ko rok raha hai. 'Thwart' ka matlab prevent ya oppose karna hota hai. 'Incubate' (develop hone dena) aur 'precipitate' (cause karna) yahan completely opposite meaning de rahe hain.
trick: Aage 'fostering atomized individualism' likha hai, jiska matlab log akele ho rahe hain. Yani interaction ko roka (thwart) ja raha hai.
tip: Individualism badhega toh interaction 'thwart' hoga.

question: Based on the passage in Question 16, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 18.
explanation: Classes ke beech aisi barriers ban gayi hain jinhe paar nahi kiya ja sakta, tabhi society fragment ho rahi hai. 'Insurmountable' ka matlab hota hai too great to be overcome. 'Permeable' (jiske aar-paar ja sakein) aur 'ephemeral' (short-lived) society ke division ki seriousness ko weak kar denge.
trick: Aage sentence mein 'exclusive enclaves' (alag-thalag societies) ka zikr hai, matlab barrier cross karna impossible hai.
tip: Class barriers ke liye strong negative adjective 'insurmountable' best hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 16, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 19.
explanation: Agar human connection ko prioritize nahi kiya, toh genuine empathy ek aisi cheez ban jayegi jo normal nahi hogi. 'Anomalous' ka matlab hota hai deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected (yaani ajeeb aur rare). 'Ubiquitous' (everywhere) aur 'quintessential' (typical example) iske opposite hain.
trick: 'Rare and...' ke baad waisa hi word aayega jo rarity ya un-naturalness show kare. Anomalous fits perfectly.
tip: Rare ke sath parallel meaning mein anomalous (abnormal) lagta hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 16, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 20.
explanation: Agar empathy aur connection khatam ho gaya, toh civic spirit (nagrikta ki bhawna) bhi dheere-dheere mar jayegi. 'Atrophy' ka matlab hota hai gradually decline in effectiveness or vigor due to underuse. 'Renascence' (rebirth), 'proliferation' (rapid increase) aur 'apotheosis' (climax) sab positive growth wale words hain.
trick: 'Slow but inevitable...' ke baad death ya decline wala word aana chahiye kyunki passage ka conclusion warning de raha hai.
tip: Civic spirit ki warning mein hamesha decline (atrophy) hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: In the realm of post-structuralist linguistics, the assumption that words possess an inherent, fixed connection to their referents is widely considered (21)_____. Thinkers like Derrida argued that meaning is perpetually deferred, emerging only through a complex web of differences rather than through direct representation. Consequently, any attempt to pin down a definitive, monolithic truth within a text is inherently (22)_____. The author's intended meaning, once considered the absolute bedrock of interpretation, is now often treated as a mere (23)_____, subservient to the myriad ways in which language can be deconstructed by the reader. This paradigm shift does not merely complicate literary critique; it profoundly (24)_____ the very foundation of epistemological certainty. If our primary tool for apprehending reality—language—is fundamentally unstable, then our grasp on reality itself must be seen as dangerously (25)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 21.
explanation: Passage post-structuralism ki baat kar raha hai jo purani soch (words ka fixed meaning hona) ko reject karta hai. 'Anachronistic' ka matlab hota hai purane zamaane ka ya outdated. 'Immutable' (unchangeable) aur 'symbiotic' (mutually beneficial) context mein fit nahi hote kyunki fixed connection ko modern thinkers galat maante hain. 'Clairvoyant' ka matlab future dekhne wala hota hai, jo irrelevant hai.
trick: Agar post-structuralist nai theory hai, toh fixed connection wali baat unke liye outdated (anachronistic) hi hogi.
tip: New theories always consider old rigid rules as anachronistic.

question: Based on the passage in Question 21, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 22.
explanation: Derrida kehte hain ki meaning fix nahi hota. Toh agar koi text mein ek fix (monolithic) truth dhoondhne ki koshish karega, toh wo koshish bewaqoofi ya impractical hogi. 'Quixotic' ka matlab highly unrealistic ya impractical hota hai. 'Pragmatic' (practical), 'prescient' (future dekhne wala) aur 'axiomatic' (self-evident/obvious truth) sab galat hain kyunki author is koshish ko reject kar raha hai.
trick: Tone negative hai attempt ke liye. Sirf 'quixotic' ek negative/impractical sense de raha hai baki sab positive hain.
tip: Impractical aur impossible attempts ke liye 'quixotic' best choice hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 21, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 23.
explanation: Pehle author ke intention ko sab kuch (bedrock) maana jata tha, par ab reader ke aage uski aukaat ek illusion jaisi reh gayi hai. 'Chimera' ka matlab illusion ya unreal dream hota hai. 'Panacea' (rambaan ilaaj), 'cornerstone' (base/foundation) aur 'fulcrum' (support) sab strong aur real cheezein hain, jabki passage iski value gira raha hai.
trick: 'Mere' (sirf) word hint deta hai ki aage aane wala word kisi cheez ki value ko downplay karega. Chimera means illusion.
tip: 'Mere' ke baad aksar weak ya illusory words aate hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 21, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 24.
explanation: Paradigm shift (soch mein badlaav) ne sirf literary critique ko complex nahi kiya, balki truth (certainty) ke foundation ko hila kar rakh diya hai. 'Destabilizes' ka matlab undermine ya weak karna. 'Crystallizes' (clear karna), 'venerates' (respect karna) aur 'amalgamates' (mix karna) yahan sense nahi banate kyunki truth ab unstable ban chuka hai.
trick: Sentence structure 'does not merely complicate... it profoundly ___' indicate karta hai ki complication se bhi bada koi disruptive action hoga.
tip: Certainty aur foundation ke against hamesha destabilize aata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 21, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 25.
explanation: Agar reality samajhne ka tool (language) hi unstable hai, toh reality par hamari pakad (grasp) bhi weak hogi. 'Tenuous' ka matlab hota hai very weak ya slight. 'Indomitable' (unbeatable), 'palpable' (tangible/clear) aur 'irrevocable' (unchangeable) sab strong words hain, jabki humein ek weak aur khatarnak state dikhani hai.
trick: 'Dangerously' word highlight karta hai ki grasp strong nahi ho sakti. Negative aur weak meaning wala word chuno.
tip: Unstable tool hamesha tenuous (weak) result deta hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The contemporary capitalist ethos operates on a brilliantly insidious logic: the manufacturing of perpetual dissatisfaction. In order to sustain the relentless engine of economic growth, the populace must be kept in a state of (26)_____ craving, constantly yearning for the next iteration of ephemeral commodities. This manufactured desire effectively (27)_____ any genuine sense of fulfillment, ensuring that the consumer remains perpetually hungry. The marketing apparatus, employing increasingly sophisticated algorithms, does not merely respond to existing needs; it actively (28)_____ them out of thin air, exploiting our deepest psychological vulnerabilities. Consequently, the act of consumption is elevated from a practical necessity to a quasi-religious ritual, offering a fleeting (29)_____ for the existential void created by modern alienation. Ultimately, this hyper-consumerist paradigm threatens to reduce human agency to mere purchasing power, leaving our moral and civic faculties critically (30)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 26.
explanation: Capitalism logon ko hamesha dissatisfied rakhta hai taaki growth chalti rahe. Iska matlab logon ki demand ya craving aisi honi chahiye jo kabhi na bujhe. 'Unquenchable' ka matlab hota hai jise satisfy na kiya ja sake. 'Perfunctory' (careless/routine), 'sporadic' (irregular) aur 'dormant' (inactive) business growth ke liye ulte pad jayenge.
trick: 'Perpetual dissatisfaction' (hamesha ki asantushti) aur 'constantly yearning' direct hint hain ki craving kabhi shant nahi hoti (unquenchable).
tip: Perpetual yearning means unquenchable desire.

question: Based on the passage in Question 26, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 27.
explanation: Yeh manufactured desire asli satisfaction ko aane hi nahi deti, tabhi toh consumer hamesha bhookha rehta hai. 'Precludes' ka matlab hota hai prevent ya make impossible. 'Expedites' (speed up), 'galvanizes' (excite/shock into action) aur 'epitomizes' (perfect example) yahan illogical hain kyunki satisfaction ko rokna zaruri hai.
trick: Agar genuine sense of fulfillment badhegi toh consumer bhookha (perpetually hungry) kaise rahega? Isliye fulfillment ko rokne (preclude) wala word chahiye.
tip: Opposite outcomes (fulfillment vs hunger) preclude se judte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 26, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 28.
explanation: Marketing sirf zaroorat puri nahi karti, wo nayi zaroorat hawa mein se paida karti hai. 'Conjures' ka matlab hota hai make something appear unexpectedly or seemingly from nowhere as if by magic. 'Mollifies' (shant karna), 'rectifies' (theek karna) aur 'interrogates' (sawaal karna) needs ko paida karne ka sense nahi dete.
trick: Phrase 'out of thin air' hamesha magic ya creation se juda hota hai. 'Conjures' iska perfect colocation hai.
tip: 'Out of thin air' ke aage humesha conjures ya creates lagta hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 26, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 29.
explanation: Shopping karna logo ki existential void (zindagi ke khali-pan) ko thodi der ke liye chupane ka kaam karta hai. 'Palliative' ka matlab aisi cheez jo problem ka root cause theek na kare, bas temporary aaram de. 'Deterrent' (rokne wala), 'catalyst' (process fast karne wala) aur 'harbinger' (sign of future) yahan fit nahi hote.
trick: 'Fleeting' (thodi der ka) ke saath medicine ya relief ka abstract term 'palliative' perfectly map hota hai jab koi deep problem (void) ho.
tip: Temporary relief for deep problems is called a palliative.

question: Based on the passage in Question 26, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 30.
explanation: Hyper-consumerism insaan ko sirf ek buyer bana deta hai, jisse uske moral aur civic dimaag par bura asar padta hai aur wo weak ho jate hain. 'Atrophied' ka matlab hota hai waste away ya decline in effectiveness. 'Bolstered' (supported), 'edified' (morally improved) aur 'vindicated' (cleared of blame) sab positive words hain.
trick: Sentence ka starting 'threatens to reduce' hai, jo ek clear negative consequence mangta hai blank ke liye. Turant sab positive options hata do.
tip: Negative cause ka effect hamesha atrophy ya decline hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: Historically, the pursuit of the 'sublime' in art demanded an engagement with the awe-inspiring and the terrifying—a deliberate confrontation with forces that (31)_____ human comprehension. However, the postmodern aesthetic landscape seems to have largely abandoned this lofty ambition, substituting profound existential inquiry with a pervasive, self-referential (32)_____. Today's avant-garde often privileges pastiche and parody over genuine innovation, resulting in cultural products that are fundamentally (33)_____, lacking any inherent, transcendent value. This shift is not merely stylistic but symptomatic of a broader cultural malaise, wherein sincere emotional expression is routinely dismissed as hopelessly (34)_____. In this cynical milieu, the artist's role transitions from a visionary truth-teller to a mere curator of recycled tropes, rendering the transformative potential of art tragically (35)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 31.
explanation: Art mein 'sublime' (mahaan ya awe-inspiring) tab hota hai jab insaan aisi forces se interact kare jo uski samajh (comprehension) se pare hon. 'Transcend' ka matlab hota hai go beyond the limits of. 'Mimic' (copy), 'elucidate' (explain) aur 'placate' (shant karna) in forces ke aage human mind ki choti aukaat ko justify nahi karte.
trick: Awe-inspiring forces hamesha human samajh ko paar (transcend) kar jati hain, explain (elucidate) ya mimic nahi karti.
tip: Forces beyond understanding always transcend human comprehension.

question: Based on the passage in Question 31, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 32.
explanation: Modern art ne serious 'existential inquiry' ko chhod diya hai aur uski jagah parody/mazak chal raha hai. 'Flippancy' ka matlab hota hai lack of respect ya seriousness. 'Gravitas' (seriousness), 'erudition' (deep knowledge) aur 'piety' (religious devotion) purani art ('sublime') ke terms hain, postmodern art ke nahi.
trick: Substitute kiya ja raha hai 'profound' (deep/serious) cheez ko. Toh substitute hamesha light ya non-serious (flippancy) hoga tone ke hisab se.
tip: Profound (serious) ka opposite flippancy (non-serious) hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 31, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 33.
explanation: Jab art sirf purani cheezon ko copy karke banti hai (pastiche and parody), toh usme apna kuch original nahi hota. 'Derivative' ka matlab hota hai imitated ya doosro se copy kiya hua. 'Germane' (relevant), 'primordial' (ancient/original) aur 'infallible' (error-free) yahan totally out of context hain.
trick: 'Privileges pastiche and parody over genuine innovation' clear bold clue hai ki art copy ho rahi hai, yani derivative hai.
tip: Lack of innovation sidhe 'derivative' word ki taraf point karta hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 31, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 34.
explanation: Aaj ke cynical time mein, agar koi sacche emotion dikhata hai toh usko mazaak samjha jata hai ya bahut purana/boring ghisa-pita mana jata hai. 'Trite' ka matlab hota hai overused ya lacking originality. 'Prescient' (prophetic), 'subversive' (rebellious) aur 'enigmatic' (mysterious) sacche emotion ke rejection ko explain nahi kar sakte.
trick: Tone cynical hai. Sincere emotion ko positively nahi dekha jayega. Un charo mein sirf 'trite' ek dismissing negative word hai.
tip: Dismissed as ke baad ek negative ya devaluing adjective aata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 31, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 35.
explanation: Artist ab sirf purani cheezein recycle kar raha hai, toh art ke andar kuch naya badlaav laane ki taakat (transformative potential) mar chuki hai. 'Inert' ka matlab hota hai lacking the ability or strength to move ya powerless. 'Catalytic' (change laane wala), 'sacrosanct' (holy) aur 'pervasive' (widespread) art ke girte hue level ko contradict kar rahe hain.
trick: 'Tragically' ek adverb hai jo strongly negative result maang raha hai. Potential ab active nahi bacha, balki 'inert' ho gaya hai.
tip: Jab potential khatam ho jaye, toh wo 'inert' ho jata hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The bedrock of any utilitarian calculus rests on the assumption that moral actions can be quantified by their net contribution to collective happiness. Yet, this ostensibly egalitarian framework frequently masks a deeply troubling (36)_____ to the rights of the marginalized minority. When the metric of societal good is exclusively tethered to the majority's preference, ethical deliberations are stripped of their normative weight, reducing justice to a mere arithmetic of utility. Such a paradigm invariably (37)_____ policies that sacrifice individual dignity on the altar of the 'greater good.' Furthermore, the very attempt to measure human suffering and joy in uniform, empirical terms is epistemologically (38)_____, as it ignores the profoundly subjective nature of lived experience. To avoid the tyrannical implications of strict utilitarianism, a robust ethical theory must (39)_____ an inviolable set of human rights that cannot be overridden by statistical imperatives. Without such safeguards, our moral compass is inherently (40)_____, vulnerable to the shifting winds of populist pragmatism. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 36.
explanation: Utilitarianism (majority ki happiness) ke faayde ke peeche ek bura sach chhupa hai ki yeh theory minority ke rights ki bilkul parwah nahi karti. 'Callousness' ka matlab cruel disregard ya insensitivity hota hai. 'Deference' (respect), 'obsequiousness' (chaploosi) aur 'magnanimity' (generosity) minority rights ke suppression wale negative context se match nahi karte.
trick: 'Deeply troubling' (pareshan karne wala) ke aage hamesha negative attitude aayega. Deference aur magnanimity toh positive hain.
tip: Minority rights ka neglect 'callousness' (insensitivity) kehlata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 36, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 37.
explanation: Yeh system aisi policies ko paida karta hai jahan ek insaan ki dignity majority ke faayde ke liye sacrifice kar di jati hai. 'Engenders' ka matlab hota hai cause or give rise to. 'Stymies' (roknna/prevent), 'castigates' (scold) aur 'nullifies' (cancel out) policies ko banane ke sense mein logical nahi hain, balki yeh word system ka result dikha raha hai.
trick: Paradigm (system) hamesha policies ko produce karta hai (engender), na ki unhe scold (castigate) karta hai.
tip: System ya paradigm policies ko 'engender' (paida) karte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 36, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 38.
explanation: Emotions (suffering/joy) ko numbers mein napna author ko ghalat lagta hai kyunki har insaan ki feeling subjective hoti hai. 'Spurious' ka matlab hota hai false, fake ya faulty logic par based. 'Irrefutable' (undeniable), 'axiomatic' (self-evident) aur 'propitious' (favorable) is action ko support karenge, jabki author iski criticism kar raha hai.
trick: Clause 'as it ignores' batata hai ki pichla statement ek mistake ya fallacy hai. Hence, faulty/false word (spurious) needed hai.
tip: Logic jo important reality ignore kare wo spurious (fake/flawed) hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 36, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 39.
explanation: Tyanny (tanashahi) se bachne ke liye, ek acche ethical theory ko human rights ko strongly protect karke secure jagah deni chahiye. 'Enshrine' ka matlab hota hai preserve in a form that ensures it will be protected and respected. 'Repudiate' (reject), 'obfuscate' (confuse) aur 'subvert' (undermine) human rights ko destroy kar denge, jo galat hai.
trick: 'Inviolable set of human rights' (jinhe toda na ja sake) aisi cheezon ko hamesha protect ya enshrine kiya jata hai.
tip: Pavitra rights hamesha law mein 'enshrine' kiye jate hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 36, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 40.
explanation: Agar rights ki protection nahi hogi, toh hamara moral compass easily corrupt ho jayega ('vulnerable to shifting winds'). 'Compromised' ka matlab hota hai weakened ya corrupted. 'Unassailable' (unbeatable), 'resilient' (strong) aur 'vindicated' (justified) sab strong position dikhate hain, par sentence condition without safeguards (weakness) ki baat kar raha hai.
trick: Without safeguards ke baad hamesha weakness (compromised) aayegi, resilience ya strength nahi.
tip: Safeguards ke bina moral compass hamesha compromised hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The phenomenological inquiry into human consciousness reveals that our subjective experience of time is rarely perfectly aligned with the rigid, tick-tock progression of mechanical clocks. Bergson posited that true 'duration' is a fluid, continuous flow, yet modern industrial society has completely (41)_____ this internal rhythm, replacing it with a rigidly quantified grid. We are coerced into perceiving time not as a lived continuity, but as a discrete series of manageable, quantifiable units. This relentless drive to spatialize time inherently (42)_____ the richness of organic memory, reducing profound personal histories to mere chronological data points. Consequently, the individual is forced to (43)_____ their most visceral, unquantifiable experiences to the margins of significance. In this hyper-rationalized paradigm, any intuitive understanding of the cosmos that defies empirical measurement is immediately dismissed as hopelessly (44)_____. Ultimately, this tragic (45)_____ of measured time with true lived experience alienates humanity from its own existential essence, trapping us in a perpetual present devoid of genuine historical depth. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 41.
explanation: Author keh raha hai ki modern society ne hamare andar ke natural time ('fluid rhythm') ko daba diya hai aur uski jagah mechanical time laa diya hai. 'Subjugated' ka matlab hota hai kisi cheez ko apne control mein karke daba dena. 'Exalted' (praise karna), 'corroborated' (confirm karna), aur 'vindicated' (justify karna) sab positive words hain, jo yahan ke extreme negative tone se match nahi karte.
trick: Sentence mein 'replacing it with a rigidly quantified grid' likha hai. Yani natural flow ko forcibly roka gaya hai. Negative dominative word chuniye.
tip: Society jab natural cheez ko control karti hai toh usko 'subjugate' karti hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 41, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 42.
explanation: Mechanical time organic memory (real yaadon) ki richness ko kharab kar raha hai. 'Vitiates' ka matlab hota hai quality ko spoil karna ya impair karna. 'Augments' (badhana), 'crystallizes' (clear karna), aur 'embellishes' (sajana) saare positive effects de rahe hain, jabki 'reducing profound personal histories' ek clear negative effect hai.
trick: 'Reducing' word aage hint de raha hai ki action negative aur destructive hai. Baki 3 options logically positive hain.
tip: Kisi achi cheez ki value girane ke liye 'vitiates' use hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 41, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 43.
explanation: Society humein force kar rahi hai ki hum apne deep emotions ko margin (kinare) par daal dein. 'Relegate' ka matlab hota hai kisi important cheez ko inferior rank ya position par dhakel dena. 'Assimilate' (mix karna), 'foreground' (important banana), aur 'transcend' (limit paar karna) yahan margin par bhejne ka logic nahi dete.
trick: 'To the margins of significance' ek direct prepositional phrase hai jo hamesha 'relegate' ya 'banish' jaise words ke sath aata hai.
tip: 'Relegate to the margins' ek standard high-level phrase hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 41, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 44.
explanation: Jo cheezein science (empirical measurement) se measure nahi ho sakti, rational society unhe bekaar ya vague maanti hai. 'Nebulous' ka matlab hota hai hazy, vague ya unclear. 'Infallible' (kabhi galat na hone wala), 'pragmatic' (practical), aur 'empirical' khud society ki pasandida cheezein hain, unhe dismiss kyun kiya jayega?
trick: Agar kisi cheez ko 'dismiss' (reject) kiya ja raha hai, toh use clear ya accurate nahi mana jayega. 'Nebulous' is the only negative/weak adjective here.
tip: Rational log unmeasurable cheezon ko humesha 'nebulous' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 41, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 45.
explanation: Author ke hisab se clock time alag hai aur real lived time alag, par log dono ko ek maanne ki ghalti kar rahe hain. 'Conflation' ka matlab hota hai do alag concepts ya cheezon ko mistakenly ek sath mix kar dena. 'Bifurcation' (divide karna), 'delineation' (clearly define karna), aur 'repudiation' (reject karna) is mix-up ko nahi batate.
trick: Passage ke start mein dono time formats ko alag bataya tha. End mein 'tragic ___ of A with B' ka matlab hai ki A aur B ko wrongly mix kar diya gaya hai.
tip: Do distinct concepts ka galat mix-up hamesha 'conflation' hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: In the labyrinthine corridors of contemporary literary theory, the traditional (46)_____ of the authorial voice has been aggressively dismantled. The notion that a text harbors a single, authoritative meaning bestowed by its creator is now viewed as an intellectual relic. Instead, the text is recognized as a (47)_____ space, a fabric woven from countless cultural citations that the reader must untangle. This theoretical emancipation, however, is not without its perils. By entirely erasing the author, we risk descending into an interpretive anarchy where all readings are considered equally valid, thereby (48)_____ the very concept of critical rigor. If a literary work is merely an empty vessel waiting to be filled by the reader's subjective biases, the text loses its power to challenge or (49)_____ our pre-existing worldviews. Thus, while the 'death of the author' liberates the reader from interpretive tyranny, it paradoxically traps them in a solipsistic echo chamber, where the text merely reflects their own (50)_____ back at them. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 46.
explanation: Pehle author ki aawaz ko sabse upar aur dominant mana jata tha, jise ab 'dismantle' ya tod diya gaya hai. 'Hegemony' ka matlab leadership ya dominance hota hai. 'Subservience' (ghulami), 'ambivalence' (confusion), aur 'marginalia' (notes in margins) author ke traditional powerful role ko define nahi karte.
trick: Author ka role pehle powerful tha, isliye 'authoritative meaning' aage likha hai. Power show karne wala ek hi word hai: Hegemony.
tip: Traditional authority ko define karne ke liye 'hegemony' sabse apt hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 46, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 47.
explanation: Ab text ko ek 'single meaning' wala nahi maana jata, balki ek aisi jagah maana jata hai jiske bahot saare meanings nikalte hain. 'Polysemic' ka matlab hota hai having many meanings. 'Monolithic' iska exact opposite hai (ek solid block jaisa). 'Didactic' (teaching purpose) aur 'sterile' (barren/empty) context se bahar hain.
trick: 'Instead' word batata hai ki pichle idea ('single meaning') ka opposite aayega. Single ka opposite poly (many) hota hai.
tip: Single meaning ka antonym post-structuralism mein 'polysemic' hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 46, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 48.
explanation: Agar sabki interpretation sahi maan li jaye (anarchy), toh serious criticism ka koi matlab hi nahi bachega. Uski aatma nikal jayegi. 'Eviscerating' ka literal matlab hota hai kisi ke andar ke organs nikaal lena, yahan iska metaphorical meaning hai kisi concept ki core strength ko destroy kar dena. Baki options ('fortifying', 'engendering') positive support de rahe hain.
trick: 'Risk descending into an interpretive anarchy' clearly ek danger (negative outcome) show kar raha hai, isliye action completely destructive hona chahiye.
tip: Critical rigor ko extreme danger mein daalne ke liye 'eviscerating' use karein.

question: Based on the passage in Question 46, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 49.
explanation: Achi literature ka kaam hamare puraane aur narrow thoughts ko todna ya challenge karna hota hai. 'Subvert' ka matlab hota hai undermine the power and authority of an established system ya belief. 'Validate', 'echo', aur 'pacify' sab comfort dene wale words hain, jo 'challenge' word ki parallel category mein fit nahi hote.
trick: 'Challenge or ___' mein 'or' ke pehle negative/aggressive verb hai, toh baad mein bhi established ideas ko todne wala aggressive word (subvert) aayega.
tip: 'Challenge' ke sath strong ideological pair 'subvert' banta hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 46, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 50.
explanation: Agar text mein reader sirf apna hi meaning dalega, toh use text mein sirf apni hi parchhai dikhegi. Ye self-obsession ki boundary hai. 'Narcissism' ka matlab hota hai excessive interest in oneself. 'Altruism' (selflessness), 'magnanimity' (generosity), aur 'objectivity' (unbiasedness) bilkul opposite hain is selfish 'echo chamber' wale environment ke.
trick: 'Solipsistic echo chamber' matlab sirf apni hi aawaz sunna. Is psychological trap ko narcissism kehte hain.
tip: Solipsistic nature hamesha narcissism ko birth deta hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The insidious genius of modern surveillance capitalism lies in its departure from overt authoritarianism; instead, it relies on a far more (51)_____ mechanism of control. We willingly embed listening devices into our sanctuaries and carry tracking beacons in our pockets, entirely seduced by the illusion of unparalleled convenience. This architecture of constant observation does not force compliance through the threat of physical violence; rather, it cultivates a profoundly (52)_____ form of self-policing. As individuals internalize the unblinking gaze of the algorithmic panopticon, they preemptively alter their behavior, ensuring they never deviate from statistically normalized parameters. The true danger of this paradigm is that it operates so seamlessly that the populace perceives their heavily curated choices as genuine expressions of (53)_____. When every desire is anticipated and monetized before it is even fully articulated, the fundamental human capacity for spontaneous, unscripted action is severely (54)_____. Ultimately, we are witnessing the silent, voluntary surrender of our cognitive sovereignty, wrapped in the deceptively benign language of personalized (55)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 51.
explanation: Modern surveillance pehle jaisa open aur direct ('overt authoritarianism') nahi hai. Ye hidden hai par bahot harmful hai. 'Pernicious' ka matlab hota hai having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. 'Obtrusive' (noticeable) galat hai kyunki ye hidden hai. 'Benevolent' (kind) aur 'archaic' (old) contextually opposite hain.
trick: 'Insidious genius' start mein likha hai. Insidious ka closest advanced synonym 'pernicious' hota hai jo hidden damage dikhata hai.
tip: Subtle aur dangerous control system ko pernicious kaha jata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 51, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 52.
explanation: Digital surveillance logo se unke andar hi ek dar paida karta hai, jisse log khud ko hi control ('self-policing') karte hain. 'Panoptic' Foucault ki philosophy ka word hai jiska matlab hai ek aisi observation jahan sab kuch continuously dekha ja raha ho, bhale hi guards saamne na hon. Baki options surveillance aur control ke mechanism se bilkul match nahi karte.
trick: Agli line mein 'algorithmic panopticon' clearly mentioned hai. Panopticon ek system hai jiska adjective panoptic hota hai.
tip: Self-policing through observation ko 'panoptic' control kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 51, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 53.
explanation: System itna clever hai ki logon ko lagta hai ki jo decisions unhone liye hain (jo ki actually algorithm ne decide kiye hain) wo unke apne azaad decisions hain. 'Autonomy' ka matlab independence ya azaadi hota hai. System control kar raha hai par logo ko 'illusion' autonomy ka hai. 'Conformity' ya 'servility' lagne par unhe danger pata chal jayega.
trick: Log is deception mein faste hain kyunki unhe lagta hai wo free hain. 'Genuine expression of...' hamesha freedom ya autonomy ke sath ata hai jab illusion dikhana ho.
tip: Fake freedom ke concept mein log 'autonomy' ka illusion paalte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 51, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 54.
explanation: Jab har desire pehle se calculate aur monetise ho jati hai, toh insaan ki khud ki natural ('spontaneous, unscripted') harkat karne ki taakat kam ho jati hai. 'Curtailed' ka matlab hota hai reduce ya restrict karna. 'Amplified' aur 'galvanized' power badhane ki baat karte hain. 'Reified' (abstract ko real banana) yahan verb format mein wrong idea de raha hai.
trick: Surveillance system hamesha human freedom ya unscripted action ko kam ('curtail') karta hai, badhata nahi.
tip: Restriction of action ke liye 'curtail' sabse precise verb hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 51, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 55.
explanation: Insaan apna dimaag tech companies ko de raha hai, lekin bahar se ye 'deceptively benign' (jhoothi acchayi) jaisa dikhta hai kyunki tech companies is control ko 'personalized experience' ya 'content sorting' bolti hain. 'Curation' ka matlab content select aur organize karna hota hai (jaise Netflix/Instagram recommendation). Subjugation, censorship, aur disenfranchisement sachchai hain, par wo 'benign language' nahi hain jo cover-up ki tarah use hoti hain.
trick: Blank ke pehle 'deceptively benign language' (dhokhebhari pyari bhasha) likha hai. 'Curation' ek harmless sounding word hai jo tech world mein control ko chupane ke liye use hota hai.
tip: 'Personalized' ke sath algorithm hamesha 'curation' word chipkate hain.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The advent of ubiquitous digital reproduction has fundamentally altered our ontological relationship with art, stripping the masterpiece of its unique, historically grounded (56)_____. When a painting can be infinitely duplicated and disseminated across millions of screens in a fraction of a second, its ritualistic value—its almost sacred presence in a specific time and space—is completely (57)_____. We no longer undertake pilgrimages to experience the transcendent power of an original work; instead, we casually consume its flattened, pixelated proxy as part of a relentless stream of digital detritus. While optimists hail this as a triumph of cultural democratization, a more cynical reading suggests it is a profound (58)_____ of the aesthetic experience. The artwork, completely divorced from its material provenance, becomes a mere floating signifier, readily appropriated for commercial or superficial ends. Consequently, our capacity for sustained, contemplative absorption is replaced by a state of distracted (59)_____, wherein art is no longer an object of reverence but a fleeting stimulus designed to elicit a momentary, (60)_____ reaction before we scroll to the next image. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 56.
explanation: Walter Benjamin ki theory par based passage hai. Original art mein ek special presence ya jadoo hota hai jo history aur space se juda hota hai. Is unique quality ko 'aura' kehte hain. Digital copy banane par ye 'aura' cheen (strip) liya jata hai. 'Stigma', 'cacophony', aur 'banality' negative terms hain jo original masterpiece ki taareef nahi kar sakte.
trick: Art ki 'unique, historically grounded' quality ko describe karna hai. 'Aura' ekmaatr word hai jo aisi mystic original presence ko capture karta hai.
tip: Mechanical reproduction ke context mein art ka 'aura' hamesha lost hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 56, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 57.
explanation: Jab masterpiece ko screen par millions baar copy kiya jata hai, toh uski sacred aur ritual value totally tabah ho jati hai. 'Obliterated' ka matlab hota hai destroyed utterly / wiped out. 'Immortalized', 'augmented' (increased), aur 'consecrated' (made sacred) positive results dikhate hain, jo author ke lamenting tone ke virodh mein hain.
trick: Blank ke pehle 'completely' word hai aur passage ka overall tone loss of value par hai. Isliye extreme destruction wala word aayega.
tip: Sacred value ka digital age mein hamesha obliteration hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 56, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 58.
explanation: Optimists ise democratization (sabke liye equal access) mante hain, par cynics isko aesthetic value ka girna mante hain. 'Debasement' ka matlab hota hai reduce in quality or value. 'Amplification' (badhna), 'synthesis' (combination), aur 'renaissance' (rebirth) art ki value girne ke concept ko fit nahi karte.
trick: Sentence mein 'While optimists hail this... a more cynical reading suggests' ka contrast hai. Agar first half positive ('triumph') hai, toh cynical reading negative (debasement) hogi.
tip: Cynics ke perspective se mass production hamesha art ka debasement hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 56, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 59.
explanation: Log ab art ko gaur se ('contemplative absorption') nahi dekhte, bas casually scroll karte hue superficial attention dete hain. 'Dilettantism' ka matlab hota hai superficially kisi art form mein interest lena bina real knowledge ya depth ke. 'Equanimity' (calmness) aur 'asceticism' (strict lifestyle) yahan irrelevent hain.
trick: Phrase 'distracted ___' ek superficial aur non-serious behavior demand karta hai. Dilettantism art ke superficial consumption ka perfect noun hai.
tip: Art ko seriously na lene aur bas time-pass samajhne ko dilettantism kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 56, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 60.
explanation: Digital screen ki art bas ek second ka shock ya feeling ('fleeting stimulus') deti hai jo dimaag tak nahi balki bas physical reflex jaisa hota hai. 'Visceral' ka matlab hota hai relating to deep inward feelings rather than to the intellect. 'Enduring' (long-lasting), 'profound' (deep), aur 'cerebral' (intellectual) wo qualities hain jo original masterpiece mein hoti hain, distracted scroll mein nahi.
trick: 'Momentary' ke sath deep intellectual response nahi aayega. Quick, physical/emotional shock ko hamesha 'visceral' kaha jata hai.
tip: Scroll karte waqt aane wala instant, unthinking reaction visceral hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The ongoing debate surrounding human volition has been fundamentally disrupted by recent neurobiological advancements, which suggest that our deeply held conviction in free will might be nothing more than a neurological (61)_____. If our cognitive processes are entirely dictated by the (62)_____ laws of biochemistry and cellular interaction, the traditional moral framework of society collapses. This deterministic worldview effectively (63)_____ individuals of true moral responsibility, rendering our justice systems archaic. Furthermore, the very (64)_____ of human dignity—the belief that we are the conscious architects of our destinies—is severely undermined. Critics argue that embracing this mechanistic view leaves humanity philosophically (65)_____, trapped in a predetermined script where personal agency is an evolutionary illusion designed merely to facilitate social cohesion. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 61.
explanation: Passage neurobiology ke context mein 'free will' ko ek illusion bata raha hai. 'Chimera' ka matlab hota hai ek illusion ya unrealisable dream. 'Panacea' (rambaan ilaaj), 'paradigm' (model), aur 'manifesto' (declaration) yahan scientific illusion wale tone ke sath match nahi karte.
trick: Sentence mein 'nothing more than' likha hai, jo aage ek negative ya fake concept ki demand karta hai. Chimera sabse apt negative word hai.
tip: False beliefs aur illusions ke liye 'chimera' use hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 61, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 62.
explanation: Biochemistry ke laws fixed hote hain aur unhe badla nahi ja sakta. 'Inexorable' ka matlab hota hai impossible to stop or prevent (jise roka ya taala na ja sake). 'Malleable' (flexible), 'capricious' (fickle/badalne wala), aur 'erratic' (unpredictable) laws ki strictness ko galat sabit kar denge.
trick: Science ke laws jo human behavior ko control karte hain, wo hamesha strict aur unstoppable hote hain. Inexorable best fit hai.
tip: Nature ya science ke strict laws hamesha 'inexorable' hote hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 61, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 63.
explanation: Agar sab kuch chemistry decide karti hai, toh insaan apne actions ke liye zimmedar nahi bacha. 'Absolves' ka matlab hota hai free from guilt or responsibility. 'Inculpates' (blame karna) iska opposite hai. 'Venerates' (respect karna) aur 'obfuscates' (confuse karna) responsibility ke context mein illogical hain.
trick: Jab actions predetermined hain, toh responsibility se chhutkara mil jata hai. Chhutkara paane ka exact legal/formal word 'absolves' hai.
tip: Responsibility ya guilt se mukt karne ko 'absolve' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 61, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 64.
explanation: Free will ko human dignity ka base ya foundation maana jata hai. 'Underpinning' ka matlab solid foundation ya basis hota hai. 'Facade' (fake front), 'anomaly' (oddity), aur 'digression' (deviation) dignity ke strong base wale context ko support nahi karte.
trick: Sentence mein aage 'the belief that we are...' diya hai jo ek fundamental strong belief hai. Fundamental foundation ko underpinning kehte hain.
tip: Kisi strong thought ya belief ka base 'underpinning' kehlata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 61, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 65.
explanation: Agar humein pata chale ki hamari koi 'agency' (power to act) nahi hai, toh humanity mentally helplessly stuck feel karegi. 'Paralyzed' ka philosophical use helpless ya unable to act hone ke liye hua hai. 'Liberated' (free) aur 'galvanized' (energized) positive terms hain. 'Exculpated' (blame se free) yahan emotion ya state of action ko nahi dikhata.
trick: Aage 'trapped in a predetermined script' likha hai. Trapped insaan humesha paralyzed feel karta hai, liberated nahi.
tip: Jab freedom of choice chhin jaye, toh insaan paralyzed feel karta hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The modern digital ecosystem exposes the global citizenry to a relentless (66)_____ of distant suffering, paradoxically eroding our capacity for genuine compassion. Constant exposure to tragedy does not amplify empathy; rather, it (67)_____ the moral senses, leading to a profound state of compassion fatigue. We experience the trauma of the 'other' strictly as a (68)_____ spectacle, safely mediated by glowing screens. This passive consumption of misery borders on ethical (69)_____, transforming profound human agony into consumable content for the scrolling masses. Consequently, the user is left feeling politically and socially (70)_____, overwhelmed by the sheer magnitude of systemic crises while completely disconnected from any actionable remedy. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 66.
explanation: Digital duniya mein humein door ke dukhon ka ek flood ya overwhelming amount dekhne ko milta hai. 'Deluge' ka matlab extreme flood ya heavy downpour hota hai (yahan information ka). 'Paucity' (kami) opposite meaning deta. 'Synthesis' (combination) aur 'moratorium' (temporary ban) totally out of context hain.
trick: 'Relentless' (lagaatar) word indicate karta hai ki kisi cheez ki bahut bhari matra aa rahi hai. Deluge is the perfect fit.
tip: Information ya suffering ke overwhelming flow ko 'deluge' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 66, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 67.
explanation: Lagaatar buri khabrein dekhne se hamari empathy badhti nahi, balki hum sunn (numb) ho jate hain. 'Anesthetizes' ka metaphorical meaning hai numb kar dena ya sensation khatam kar dena. 'Sensitizes' iska exact opposite hai. 'Exacerbates' (worsen) aur 'placates' (pacify) yahan emotional numbness ko nahi darshate.
trick: Sentence mein 'does not amplify... rather it ___' likha hai. Amplify ka ulta ya compassion fatigue lane wala word anesthetizes hi hai.
tip: Constant trauma dekhne se moral senses 'anesthetize' (sunn) ho jate hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 66, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 68.
explanation: Hum screens ke through dusro ka dukh indirectly experience karte hain. 'Vicarious' ka matlab hota hai experienced in the imagination through the feelings or actions of another person. 'Empirical' (observation based), 'visceral' (deep inward feeling), aur 'somatic' (physical body se related) direct experiences hain, jabki screen ka experience indirect hota hai.
trick: 'Safely mediated by glowing screens' saaf batata hai ki experience direct nahi hai, secondary hai. Vicarious means secondary/indirect experience.
tip: Dusro ke through feel kiye gaye emotion ko 'vicarious' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 66, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 69.
explanation: Dusro ke dukh ko safely screen par ek content ki tarah consume karne ko author ek buri aadat bata raha hai. 'Voyeurism' ka matlab hota hai dusro ki suffering ya private cheezon ko dekh kar abnormal pleasure ya interest lena. 'Altruism' aur 'philanthropy' selfless help ko kehte hain, jo yahan passage ke negative tone ke khilaf hain.
trick: Passive consumption of misery ek negative act hai. Sirf voyeurism is list mein ek creepy aur negative consumption ko dikhata hai.
tip: Dusro ka dukh secretly/safely dekhna 'voyeurism' kahlata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 66, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 70.
explanation: Insaan itni saari buri khabrein dekh kar helpless aur powerless feel karta hai, kyunki wo kuch theek nahi kar sakta. 'Impotent' ka yahan abstract matlab hai powerless ya unable to take effective action. 'Omnipotent' (all-powerful) bilkul opposite hai. 'Resilient' (tough) aur 'catalytic' (change laane wala) active words hain jo helpless user par fit nahi hote.
trick: 'Disconnected from actionable remedy' matlab user kuch kar nahi sakta. Powerless state ko impotent kehte hain.
tip: Jab action lena impossible ho, toh feeling 'impotent' hoti hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The contemporary cultural landscape is dominated by a pervasive (71)_____ of the past, wherein historical epochs are endlessly recycled into marketable aesthetics. This hyper-nostalgia, however, does not foster a genuine connection to history; instead, it offers a deeply (72)_____ version of events, stripped of their original political and social friction. By commodifying historical struggles, this phenomenon effectively (73)_____ the radical potential of the past to critique the present. What remains is an (74)_____ simulation, a comforting retro-illusion designed to distract from the anxieties of the modern age. Ultimately, this obsession with curated nostalgia induces a collective cultural (75)_____, preventing society from envisioning any radically divergent future. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 71.
explanation: Aaj ka culture past ko over-glorify karke ek marketable trend bana raha hai. 'Fetishization' ka matlab kisi cheez ke liye abnormal obsession ya usko sirf aesthetic object ki tarah treat karna hota hai. 'Repudiation' (rejection) aur 'vilification' (bura-bhala kehna) past ke recycle hone ki positive-yet-hollow attraction ko explain nahi karte. 'Exegesis' (critical explanation) is tone mein nahi fit hota.
trick: Aage 'hyper-nostalgia' aur 'marketable aesthetics' likha hai. Kisi cheez ko market aesthetic banana uski fetishization kahlata hai.
tip: Past ka unhealthy obsession 'fetishization' kehlata hai modern theory mein.

question: Based on the passage in Question 71, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 72.
explanation: History se jab uski harsh realities ('social friction') nikaal di jayein, toh wo fake aur saaf-suthri lagne lagti hai. 'Sanitized' ka yahan metaphoric meaning hai 'made more palatable by removing elements that are likely to be unacceptable or controversial'. 'Authentic' bilkul opposite hai. 'Convoluted' (complex) aur 'visceral' (raw/intense) original history ke traits hote hain, retro-illusion ke nahi.
trick: 'Stripped of their original political friction' matlab history ke kaante nikal diye gaye hain. Is process ko sanitize karna kehte hain.
tip: Bure sach ko chhupa kar present karna 'sanitize' karna hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 71, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 73.
explanation: Jab history ko commodify karte hain, toh present ko challenge karne ki history ki taakat (radical potential) khatam ho jati hai. 'Neuters' ka matlab hota hai to render ineffective ya power chheen lena. 'Galvanizes' (excite into action), 'resurrects' (punarjeevit karna), aur 'bolsters' (support karna) sab power badhane wale positive words hain.
trick: Potential ko destroy karne ki baat ho rahi hai kyunki culture fake nostalgia mein dooba hai. Sirf 'neuters' ek weakening verb hai.
tip: Kisi ki power ya impact khatam karne ko 'neuter' karna kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 71, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 74.
explanation: Jo version hume becha ja raha hai wo harmless, inoffensive aur distraction ke liye hai. 'Anodyne' ka matlab hota hai not likely to provoke dissent or offense; inoffensive, often deliberately so (aur aaram dene wala). 'Subversive' (rebellious) aur 'polemical' (controversial) toh original history hoti hai. 'Sacrosanct' (holy) simulation ke context mein set nahi hota.
trick: 'Comforting retro-illusion' likha hai. Comfort dene wala aur pain hide karne wala word anodyne (painkiller) hai.
tip: Comforting aur harmless fake cheezon ko 'anodyne' kaha jata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 71, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 75.
explanation: Passage ka conclusion hai ki fake nostalgia humein future dekhne se rokti hai, yani ek memory loss ya bhoolne ki bimari jaisa effect deti hai. 'Amnesia' ka matlab loss of memory hai (yahan cultural memory loss). 'Enlightenment' (knowledge), 'prescience' (future dekhna), aur 'hypermnesia' (abnormally sharp memory) is negative conclusion ko contradict karte hain.
trick: Fake history yaad rakhne se hum real history aur future bhool jate hain. Bhoolne ko society ke level par amnesia kehte hain.
tip: Society jab history bhool jaye toh usko cultural 'amnesia' kehte hain.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: When confronted with the sheer magnitude of existential dread, human language often proves tragically inadequate, revealing the boundaries of what is genuinely (76)_____. Our vocabulary, evolved primarily for pragmatic survival and social navigation, (77)_____ the vastness of subjective despair into neat, communicable but fundamentally hollow categories. Any attempt to fully articulate the abyss of the human condition often devolves into meaningless (78)_____, where words merely loop back upon themselves without capturing the essence of the void. This linguistic (79)_____ forces the philosopher to confront the grim reality that the most profound dimensions of existence lie beyond the reach of semantics. Ultimately, we must acknowledge that at the very edge of comprehension, the only honest philosophical response is a reverent (80)_____. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 76.
explanation: Passage existential dread (bade darr) ki baat kar raha hai jise language samjha nahi sakti. 'Ineffable' ka matlab hota hai too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words. 'Palpable' (tangible), 'quotidian' (daily/ordinary), aur 'prosaic' (commonplace/boring) deep philosophical unexplainable feelings ko describe nahi karte.
trick: Sentence khud keh raha hai 'language often proves inadequate'. Jo language mein describe na ho sake, wo hamesha ineffable hota hai.
tip: Words mein describe na hone wali deep cheez 'ineffable' hoti hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 76, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 77.
explanation: Hamari bhasha hamare bade dukh ('vastness of subjective despair') ko choti aur hollow categories mein daba deti hai ya compress kar deti hai. 'Constricts' ka matlab make narrower ya limit karna hota hai. 'Expands' (badhana) aur 'illuminates' (roshni dalna) language ki weakness ke idea ko virodh karte hain. 'Distills' (purify) ek positive sense deta hai, jo hollow categories ke sath match nahi hota.
trick: Vastness (vishaalta) ko neat/choti categories mein fit karne ke liye usko squeeze ya constrict karna padta hai.
tip: Vast ideas ko narrow categories mein dalna 'constrict' karna hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 76, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 78.
explanation: Jab words abyss (gehrai) ko samjha nahi paate, toh wo bas apne aap ko repeat karne lagte hain. 'Tautology' ka matlab hota hai saying of the same thing twice in different words, jiska koi real meaning nahi banta. 'Paradox' (contradiction), 'panacea' (cure-all), aur 'heuristic' (trial-and-error method) words ke loop back hone wale meaning ko convey nahi karte.
trick: 'Words merely loop back upon themselves' ek clear definition hai Tautology ki (circular logic ya redundancy).
tip: Words ka khud pe loop back hona logical 'tautology' kehlata hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 76, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 79.
explanation: Passage ki starting se le kar ab tak yahi baat chal rahi hai ki language helpless aur weak hai. 'Impotence' ka yahan abstract meaning hai weakness ya inability to take action/express. 'Mastery', 'fluidity', aur 'clairvoyance' (future seeing) sab positive aur strong words hain jo language ki is nakami par set nahi hote.
trick: Language ka inadequate hona, constrict karna, aur fail hona... yeh sab uski powerlessness ya impotence ko dikhata hai.
tip: Language ki inexpressive nature ko uski linguistic impotence kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 76, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 80.
explanation: Wittgensteinian philosophy ka reference hai: jahan language fail ho jaye aur hum samajh ki aakhri limit par khade hon, wahan sabse honest response chup rehna hota hai. 'Silence' is context mein perfect hai. 'Cacophony' (harsh noise), 'dialectic' (debate), aur 'soliloquy' (talking to oneself) sab words involve karte hain, jo us limit par bekaar hain.
trick: Pura passage keh raha hai ki words fail ho jate hain. Jab words fail hote hain, toh honest response sirf silence hi bacha hai.
tip: Jab language inadequate ho, tab aakhri rasta philosophical 'silence' hota hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: The contemporary architecture of algorithmic governance has effectively (81)_____ the traditional boundaries between the public sphere and private sanctuary. We are no longer merely observed; our psychological profiles are preemptively synthesized by digital apparatuses that operate with a chilling, (82)_____ efficiency. This phenomenon, far from being perceived as an Orwellian nightmare, is often eagerly embraced by the populace under the (83)_____ of bespoke convenience and frictionless living. Consequently, the civic subject is transformed into a pliant data-point, willingly subjugating their autonomy to opaque systems of algorithmic sorting. What makes this paradigm uniquely insidious is its (84)_____ nature; it does not demand overt submission but rather cultivates an environment where resistance feels not only futile but inherently (85)_____, as if choosing privacy is an anti-social act. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 81.
explanation: Passage ka tone dark aur critical hai. Author keh raha hai ki public aur private life ke beech ki jo boundary thi, usko algorithms ne puri tarah khatam kar diya hai. 'Obliterated' ka matlab hota hai completely destroy karna ya mita dena. 'Demarcated' (mark karna), 'fortified' (strong banana), aur 'delineated' (outline karna) boundaries ko strong ya clear banate hain, jo passage ke tone ke opposite hai.
trick: Sentence mein privacy ke khatam hone ka hint 'no longer merely observed' mein chhipa hai. Aise extreme negative context mein destructive verb 'obliterated' hi fit baithega.
tip: Boundaries mitne (destroy) ke context mein 'obliterated' sabse strong option hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 81, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 82.
explanation: Algorithms ek aisi efficiency ke sath kaam karte hain jise roka nahi ja sakta aur jo lagatar chalti rehti hai. 'Inexorable' ka matlab hota hai impossible to stop or prevent. 'Haphazard' (unorganized) aur 'erratic' (unpredictable) algorithms ke system se match nahi karte kyunki wo highly efficient hain. 'Benign' (harmless/kind) 'chilling' (darawna) word ke bilkul opposite hai.
trick: 'Chilling' ke theek baad ek strong, powerful aur thoda negative/unstoppable tone wala word aana chahiye. Inexorable best fit hai.
tip: Unstoppable aur relentless machine logic ke liye 'inexorable' word use karein.

question: Based on the passage in Question 81, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 83.
explanation: Log is surveillance ko nightmare nahi maante kyunki unhe lagta hai yeh 'convenience' (aaram) hai. Yani asal khatra convenience ke bhesh mein aata hai. 'Guise' ka matlab hota hai external appearance jo sachai ko chhupata ho (jaise bhesh badalna). 'Repudiation' (rejection), 'clarion' (clear call), aur 'indictment' (aarop) yahan fake appearance ka logic nahi de paate.
trick: Phrase 'under the ___ of' ek standard collocation hai. Jab koi buri cheez achi bankar aati hai toh hamesha 'under the guise of' lagta hai.
tip: Buri cheez jab achi bankar aaye toh 'guise' (bhesh) word chunein.

question: Based on the passage in Question 81, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 84.
explanation: Is naye system ki sabse khatarnak baat ye hai ki ye openly saamne se attack nahi karta ('does not demand overt submission'). Ye chupke se kaam karta hai. 'Surreptitious' ka matlab hota hai secret ya stealthy. 'Coercive' (forceful) toh 'overt' ho jayega. 'Palpable' (clear/tangible) aur 'egalitarian' (equal) context mein completely illogical hain.
trick: 'Does not demand overt (open) submission' ka ulta meaning blank mein aayega, yani open ka ulta secret (surreptitious).
tip: Overt (open) ka virodhabhas hamesha secret (surreptitious) hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 81, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 85.
explanation: Privacy mangna aaj ke data-driven time mein ek anti-social aur outdated cheez maani jati hai. 'Anachronistic' ka matlab hota hai apne time se purana (out of date) lagna. 'Laudable' (praise worthy), 'vanguard' (leading position), aur 'pragmatic' (practical) privacy ki maang ko positive banate hain, jabki society ise negative/'futile' maan rahi hai.
trick: 'Futile' (bekaar) aur 'anti-social' ke sath ek negative/outdated idea hi parallel chalega. Baki teeno options purely positive hain.
tip: Old aur outdated thought process ko 'anachronistic' kaha jata hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: In the realm of post-structuralist critique, the assumption that a literary text possesses a stable, intrinsic meaning is considered hopelessly (86)_____. Derridean thought posits that meaning is perpetually deferred, rendering any quest for a singular authorial intent not just futile, but theoretically (87)_____. The text is viewed not as a monolith of absolute truth, but as a deeply fragmented landscape, teeming with internal contradictions and irreconcilable (88)_____. Consequently, the reader is elevated from a passive recipient to an active co-creator, tasked with the (89)_____ labor of unravelling the myriad cultural codes embedded within the prose. This theoretical shift, however, risks descending into absolute interpretive anarchy, where the rigorous evaluation of literature is entirely (90)_____ by radical subjectivity, leaving us in a void where every reading is equally valid and thus equally meaningless. || Question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 86.
explanation: Post-structuralism purani soch ko manta nahi hai. Ye soch ki ek text ka fix meaning hota hai, ab bahut purani aur bekar mani jati hai. 'Archaic' ka matlab hota hai old-fashioned ya outdated. 'Axiomatic' (self-evident truth), 'infallible' (never wrong), aur 'clairvoyant' (future dekhne wala) modern theory ke hisab se is purani soch par fit nahi baithte.
trick: 'Hopelessly' ke baad ek negative word aayega jo dikhaye ki ye idea reject ho chuka hai. Archaic sabse apt negative criticism hai purani theories ke liye.
tip: Old theories ko naye critics hamesha 'archaic' ya outdated bulate hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 86, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 87.
explanation: Author ka single meaning dhoondhne ki koshish na sirf futile (bekar) hai, balki theory ke hisab se jhoothi aur galat logic par based hai. 'Spurious' ka matlab hota hai false ya fake. 'Empirical' (based on observation), 'robust' (strong), aur 'propitious' (favorable) sab positive terms hain aur yahan galat logic dete hain.
trick: Phrase 'not just futile, but theoretically ___' dikhata hai ki 'futile' se bhi bada aur jyada negative attack aane wala hai. Spurious perfect hai.
tip: Futile attempt theory ki bhasha mein aksar 'spurious' (false) hota hai.

question: Based on the passage in Question 86, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 88.
explanation: Post-structuralism manta hai ki text ke andar bahut saare conflicts aur dead-ends hote hain jinhe solve nahi kiya ja sakta ('irreconcilable'). 'Aporias' (plural of aporia) ek literary term hai jiska matlab hota hai unresolvable internal contradiction ya logical puzzle. 'Convergences' (milna), 'axioms' (truths), aur 'panaceas' (cure-all) in contradictions ko ulta define kar rahe hain.
trick: 'Internal contradictions and irreconcilable ___' mein and ke baad contradiction jaisa hi (parallel) word aayega. Aporia ka matlab hi deep contradiction hota hai.
tip: Irreconcilable (unsolvable) text contradictions ko hamesha 'aporias' kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 86, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 89.
explanation: Reader ko active co-creator ban kar cultural codes ko suljhana parta hai. Ye kaam bahut mehnat aur effort wala hai. 'Herculean' ka matlab hota hai requiring great strength or effort. 'Perfunctory' (careless/routine), 'ephemeral' (short-lived), aur 'dormant' (inactive) is bade aur mushkil kaam (labor) ko galat tarike se chhota dikhate hain.
trick: 'Tasked with... labor of unravelling myriad (countless) codes' se pata chalta hai ki task bahut bada aur mushkil hai. Herculean fits perfectly.
tip: Bade aur bhari mentally demanding task ko 'herculean' labor kehte hain.

question: Based on the passage in Question 86, select the most appropriate option for blank No. 90.
explanation: Agar har reader ki baat ko sahi maan liya jaye, toh strict aur deep evaluation (rigorous evaluation) ki value khatam ho jayegi aur anarchy aa jayegi. 'Subverted' ka matlab hota hai undermine ya kisi established system ko destroy karna. 'Galvanized' (energize karna), 'edified' (moral improvement), aur 'vindicated' (justify karna) evaluation ko strong banayenge, jo is risk ke completely khilaf hai.
trick: Sentence mein aage 'leaving us in a void' likha hai (jahan sab meaningless hai). Yani pehle wale system ko destroy kiya gaya hai. Subverted = destroy power.
tip: Interpretive anarchy hamesha rigorous evaluation ko 'subvert' (todti) karti hai.

question: Direction: Read the passage and fill in the blanks. || Passage: Late-stage capitalism exhibits a terrifying genius for absorbing its own critiques, seamlessly transforming counter-cultural rebellion into yet another highly (91)_____ lifestyle brand. explanation: Capitalism ki ye khasiyat hai ki wo apne khilaf aawaz (rebellion) ko bhi ek product bana kar paise kama leta hai. 'Lucrative' ka matlab hota hai producing a great deal of profit. 'Altruistic' (selfless) capitalism se match nahi karta. 'Esoteric' (understood by few) aur 'ephemeral' (short-lived) brand ki commercial success ko define nahi kar paate.
trick: Capitalism 'lifestyle brand' banakar humesha profit hi dhundhta hai. Profit se seedha juda word 'lucrative' hai.
